title: cheapest one way car rental
answer: To find the cheapest one way car rental for a U.S. trip, compare the final totals for the same pickup station, return station, dates and car category. Check whether a one-way charge is included before paying. Avis says most locations charge no separate drop fee; Enterprise says any applicable drop charge is disclosed during reservation. Neither statement identifies the cheapest quote for your route.
html:
U.S. comparison method · Official pages reviewed October 26, 2026 · No booking test performed

What the official pages actually settle

Company and official sourcePublished charging explanationWhat it does not confirm
Avis: one-way serviceIts FAQ says most locations have no separate drop-off or one-way fee. It directs renters to review fees at step three of reservation; location pricing can differ.No fixed nationwide amount or cheapest supplier for your trip. No separate fee does not mean the rental rate matches a round trip.
Enterprise: one-way serviceA drop charge concerns returning to another location. The amount depends on location and season, and an applicable charge is disclosed during reservation.No universal drop-charge figure and no confirmation that the final total for your route has already been captured.

These are two different published explanations, not interchangeable price guarantees. Both pages were read on October 26, 2026. We did not obtain priced reservations, so we cannot name a cheapest company or publish a tested saving.

Download the route and checkout comparison worksheet (CSV)

A checkout experience worth separating from the rule

A public discussion titled “Shown the specific price for a specific rental from a specific place at a specific time to a specific destination..... but the ACTUAL price turned out to be 5x!” describes a Japanese rental search. That is the poster’s account, not a U.S. fee schedule or an independently tested price.

“moral of the story here is always go to the checkout step to see every applicable fees. Same with airbnb/agoda/airlines”

This is one commenter’s advice in that discussion in r/assholedesign. It is useful as a check to perform, not proof that every supplier adds a late charge. The quoted experience motivates the worksheet below; the official pages above establish only their own published charging explanations.

Reconcile the route, the fee and the final total

Start with one fixed journey, not a company ranking. Write the exact collection and return stations beside the dates and times. Keep the car category, driver details and intended extras unchanged across quotes. If you test a nearby station or another day, save it as a new scenario. Otherwise, a lower number may simply price a different journey.

Save three views of each proposal: the initial result, the final pre-payment breakdown and the terms for the selected route. Give them the same reference in the worksheet. A comparison needs a traceable explanation of what changed, not just two screenshots with different totals. No reservation or payment is needed to organize information already displayed to you.

Separate a missing line from a zero line. If the breakdown explicitly includes the drop charge in its total, record that wording and do not add the charge again. If the breakdown is silent, write not confirmed and ask the supplier. Silence does not establish that the route is fee-free.

Our comparison formula is: comparable trip cost = quoted rental charges + separately itemized mandatory charges + selected optional costs. Include every amount only once. Keep a refundable security authorization outside this spending total and record it separately as a funds requirement. This is a worksheet convention, not a promise about a provider’s billing.

When the total changes, find the line that changed

For a changed checkout total, calculate the difference only after matching the itinerary and selections. Difference = final displayed total minus initial displayed total. Then label each explanation supplied by the breakdown: a route charge, a changed rental charge, taxes or an extra you selected. An unexplained remainder stays unexplained. Do not label the entire difference a drop fee.

Compare coupon and no-coupon proposals on separate rows for the same journey. Record whether each total already includes the route charge and whether its payment or cancellation terms differ. A visibly accepted code is not enough to establish a saving. The useful result is a lower comparable total with conditions you can actually meet.

If returning to the original station looks cheaper, add the real cost of that alternative journey only when you have a source for it. Keep extra travel, parking and accommodation separate from the rental quote. Without those inputs, show two unranked scenarios rather than claiming that the detour saves money.

Before paying, ask one precise question about any gap: does this final total include every mandatory charge for returning this car to the named station? Save the reply with the dated quote. If the reply and the breakdown disagree, preserve both and request clarification; do not quietly replace one with the version you prefer.

Answers before checkout

Does no drop fee mean the cheapest one-way rental? No conclusion follows from that line alone. The comparison still needs the rental charge and every other applicable cost for the same journey. The table is a policy comparison, not a priced ranking.

Can I multiply the advertised daily price by the number of days? That arithmetic does not establish a reservation total when the display leaves fees or billing conditions unresolved. Use the quoted full-trip amount and itemization instead.

What if I cannot find a one-way charge in the breakdown? Record not confirmed rather than zero. Ask whether it is included, absent or still to be quoted for the named return station.

Is this the under-25 route guide? No. Our young-driver one-way guide addresses eligibility and return approval. This page addresses reconciling one-way charges. For a longer itinerary, use the full-stay rental comparison alongside your route quote.

Use the sheet to leave checkout with a total you can explain, not a claim that one brand is always cheapest. Official information comes from the linked company pages, read October 26, 2026; the formulas and reconciliation method are our editorial analysis. No rental was booked or purchased. Prices and policies can change. Confirm the current quote and agreement before payment.
